market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Mozzarella vs. cheddar: protein, fat and calories

seo.title: Mozzarella vs. cheddar: protein, fat and calories
seo.meta_description: Cheddar is more calorie- and fat-dense than whole-milk mozzarella, while the protein difference is modest. Compare per 100 g and a 1-ounce serving.

excerpt: USDA references put whole-milk mozzarella near 300 calories, 22.2 g protein and 22.4 g fat per 100 g, versus roughly 403 calories, 24.9 g protein and 33.1 g fat for cheddar. Cheddar has only about 2.7 g more protein but roughly 11 g more fat per 100 g.
content_html:
Mozzarella and cheddar both provide concentrated dairy protein, but cheddar packs substantially more fat into the same weight.

Per 100 g

Whole-milk mozzarellaCheddar
Calories~300~403
Protein~22.2 g~24.9 g
Fat~22.4 g~33.1 g
Calcium~500 mg~710 mg

Cheddar supplies only about 12% more protein but nearly 50% more fat.

One ounce makes the difference easier to picture

At 28 g, mozzarella works out to roughly 84 calories and 6.2 g protein; cheddar about 113 calories and 7.0 g protein. Less than 1 g of extra protein comes with about 29 additional calories.

Why cheddar is denser

Cheddar is pressed and aged, losing water. Mozzarella retains more moisture, especially fresh versions. Less water concentrates protein, fat, minerals and calories.

Water concentrates the difference before fat even enters the picture

Cheddar is a drier, aged cheese; fresh mozzarella retains much more water. At 100 g, removing water concentrates almost everything else—protein, fat, sodium and energy. Part of cheddar's apparent protein advantage is therefore a concentration effect.

A 30 g serving makes the absolute differences smaller and better reflects how cheese is often eaten. Low-moisture mozzarella also comes closer to cheddar than fresh mozzarella does, so the cheese name alone is not enough to predict the nutrition panel.

Mozzarella itself varies

Fresh mozzarella packed in whey or brine is not nutritionally identical to low-moisture shredded mozzarella. If calories or sodium are important, compare the exact Nutrition Facts panels rather than using one category number.

For lower energy density, mozzarella often wins; for protein, the gap is much smaller than the calorie gap.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Cheddar slightly: about 24.9 versus 22.2 g/100 g in these references.

faq.question: Does fresh mozzarella change the comparison?
faq.answer: Yes. Its higher moisture can make it significantly less calorie-dense than low-moisture mozzarella.
